provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — exploitation of CVE-2021-26855 on Exchange is a strong detection surface: IIS/Exchange request logs, W3SVC anomalies, unexpected child processes of w3wp.exe/UMWorkerProcess, webshell writes to Exchange web roots, and version/patch-state monitoring all apply
high — file-integrity monitoring on Exchange/IIS web roots (inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client) and anomalous file writes by w3wp.exe are high-fidelity, actor-relevant detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe spawning from a service process or from batch installers, and cmd.exe /c children of the Sponsor service binary, are directly observable via process-creation telemetry (Event ID 4688 / Sysmon 1)
medium — the specific 'install' command-line argument on the Sponsor binary is a detectable string in process-creation logs, but requires knowing the binary name/argument pattern

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — service creation (Event ID 7045 / 4697) with the names SystemNetwork or Update pointing at an unsigned binary in an unusual path is a high-fidelity, actor-specific detection
high — services.exe launching an unsigned backdoor binary from a non-standard path is observable via service-start and process-lineage telemetry
medium — the on-disk config files (config.txt, node.txt, error.txt) co-located with the service binary are a detectable file-artifact pattern, though the decode logic itself is in-memory
medium — high-entropy config files adjacent to a service binary are detectable via file-entropy analytics, but need dedicated scanning

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: high — a CSRSS.EXE running from a path other than %WINDIR%\System32 (or with a non-Microsoft signature) is a rare, high-fidelity masquerade detection via image-path/signature analytics
medium — reuse of local credentials is detectable via anomalous local-logon analytics but blends with legitimate administration
high — procdump against lsass.exe (command line containing lsass / -ma) and process access to lsass by Mimikatz are highly observable via EDR process-access and command-line telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: high — WebBrowserPassView execution and its access to browser credential stores (Login Data files) are detectable via known-tool hashes/signatures and file-access telemetry

medium — the discovery happens inside the backdoor via API calls rather than spawned commands, so it is subtle; detection leans on catching the backdoor process/beacon rather than the enumeration itself
medium — execution of host2ip.exe (a non-standard utility) and bursts of name-resolution/host enumeration are detectable via process and DNS telemetry
medium — internal service discovery / connection fan-out is detectable via east-west network analytics, though it can blend with legitimate scanning tools

high — periodic HTTP/80 beacons from a service process to the known Sponsor C2 IPs are detectable via network/proxy telemetry and beacon-interval analytics, especially when correlated with the C2 IOCs
medium — RC4-encrypted payloads inside plain HTTP produce high-entropy bodies over port 80 that can be flagged heuristically, but confirmation needs payload inspection
medium — Base64-encoded blobs in HTTP request/response bodies to the Sponsor C2 are detectable heuristically, particularly combined with the beacon interval and C2 IOCs
medium — obfuscated C2 is best caught via anomaly on the HTTP/80 channel to the Sponsor C2 IPs rather than content signatures

high — the Sponsor service or a URLDownloadToFileW call fetching an executable followed by its execution is detectable via process+network+file-write correlation; outbound to the tool-delivery IOCs (5.255.97.172, 198.144.189.74) adds fidelity
high — execution of RevSocks/GOST/Chisel (by known hash or renamed CSRSS.EXE outside System32) and their outbound reverse-proxy connections are detectable via process and network telemetry
high — plink.exe/gost.exe/chisel.exe execution and their tunneling connections are detectable via process command-line and outbound-connection telemetry
medium — plink.exe execution and outbound SSH from unusual internal hosts are detectable via process and network telemetry, though SSH can be legitimate in some environments
medium — outbound data returned over the beacon channel is detectable as part of the C2 flow to the Sponsor IOCs, but distinguishing exfil volume from beaconing requires flow analysis

medium — execution of Uninstall.bat and deletion of the service binary/config files (config.txt, node.txt, error.txt) are detectable via process-creation and file-delete telemetry if captured before cleanup completes
medium — execution of a non-standard sqlextractor.exe and bulk local database reads are detectable via process and file/DB-access telemetry, though it can resemble legitimate DBA activity

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim internet-wide scanning is not endpoint-observable; inbound probes may register at the perimeter but attribution to this actor is weak; hunt/intel candidate via external attack-surface monitoring
low — malware development occurs off-victim; the resulting binaries are where detection lands; intel/hunt candidate via sample tracking and YARA over the Sponsor family
low — tool acquisition itself is off-endpoint; downstream execution of each tool is the detection surface; intel/hunt candidate

hunting_candidates.technique_name: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — locale/timezone queries are in-process and indistinguishable from benign activity; hunt candidate only in the context of the backdoor
low — a single PID lookup inside the backdoor is not meaningfully observable on its own; hunt candidate tied to the backdoor
